newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's NKBM bank seen buying into HBB bank.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's NKBM bank seen buying into HBB bank.

text.p: Slovenia's third-largest bank, state-owned Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor (NKBM), may take over a third of Hipotekarna Banka Brezice (HBB), the country's Bank Rehabilitation Agency said on Wednesday .

"NKBM may take over about 1.3 billion tolars ($9.4 million) or a third of HBB's assets and an adequate share of its liabilities," Slavko Jamnik, the head of the agency which holds all of NKBM's shares, told Reuters.
Privately-owned HBB is one of Slovenia's smallest banks.
Jamnik said the exact share of liabilities that NKBM may assume as a price for its stake in HBB were still subject to negotiations and that no final decision had yet been made.
NKBM was interested in buying into HBB because doing so would enable it to establish a bank office in the town of Brezice near the Croatian border where HBB is located, Jamnik said.
NKBM's total assets stood at 168.5 billion tolars at the end of 1995. HBB's assets are at 4.3 billion tolars.

A number of the country's 29 registered banks have over the past months announced merger plans aimed at cutting operational costs and increase efficiency as banks prepare for tougher competition once the sector is thrown open to foreign players.

Parliament is expected to pass a new banking law next year, enabling foreign banks to establish branches in Slovenia in line with European Union regulations. --Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386 61 1253 644
